key_insight: Wat3R shows that underwater 3D reconstruction can be learned without expensive underwater annotations by transferring knowledge from air-domain models. It uses semi-supervised cross-domain adaptation to make feed-forward 3D geometry estimation practical in challenging aquatic environments.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of large-scale, high-quality 3D annotations for underwater scenes, where light attenuation and scattering make standard 3D learning methods difficult to apply.
method: Adapts a feed-forward 3D reconstruction model trained on air-domain data to underwater scenes.
Uses a cross-domain semi-supervised learning framework to reduce dependence on underwater ground-truth labels.
Leverages annotation-free or annotation-light adaptation to handle underwater image degradation and domain shift.
impact: This matters because it lowers the cost and data burden of building underwater 3D perception systems. For practitioners, it offers a more scalable path to deploy geometry estimation in robotics, marine inspection, and environmental monitoring.

paper_title: Wat3R: Underwater 3D Geometry Learning without Annotations
paper_authors: Jiangwei Ren, Xingyu Jiang, Zijie Song, Wei Xu, Hongkai Lin
